subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should Telegram reaction control use the shared queue/wake/off notificationWake.reactions policy, a Telegram-specific reactionSemantics map, or stay passive until a broader cross-channel design is selected?
rationale: The remaining work adds user-facing wake/config semantics and overlaps with open PRs that choose different API shapes; automation should not select that product contract for maintainers.

options.title: Adopt Shared Wake Policy
options.body: Use a shared queue-by-default notificationWake.reactions contract, add Telegram stable reaction keys, and keep per-emoji meanings outside the transport layer unless a later product surface owns them.

options.title: Use Telegram Semantics Map
options.body: Accept a Telegram-specific reactionSemantics config that maps selected emoji to actions, with explicit upgrade and docs burden for a channel-owned behavior contract.

options.title: Defer Reaction Wakes
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events for now and pause overlapping implementation PRs until maintainers want this control surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Wake Policy
recommendation.body: Use a shared queue-by-default notificationWake.reactions contract, add Telegram stable reaction keys, and keep per-emoji meanings outside the transport layer unless a later product surface owns them.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the open shared-policy candidate and has the strongest recent history across the Telegram reaction and notification wake surfaces.
